market_summary: US stocks closed mixed on November 13 with the Dow up 0.1%, S&P 500 down 0.4%, and Nasdaq down 0.91%, as technology stocks lagged while consumer staples and energy led. The major driver was Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation following personal scandal allegations, sending the chipmaker's stock down 2% and below its $4 trillion market cap. Tesla meanwhile began consumer sales of its Cybercab robotaxi at $29,990, while winding down Cybertruck production. Singapore's Singtel posted better-than-expected underlying profit growth of 10%, lifting shares 3% to their best day in three months.

items.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns After Affairs with Alleged Chinese Spy
items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO and board member effective immediately after reports of two affairs, one involving an alleged Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO while board searches for permanent replacement.

items.headline: Nvidia Stock Falls Below $4 Trillion Market Cap on Huang Fallout
items.summary: Nvidia shares fell 2% on Friday following Jensen Huang's resignation, closing below $4 trillion in market capitalization for the first time since July 2025.

items.headline: Tesla Opens Cybercab Sales for Personal Use
items.summary: Tesla began inviting select customers to order the Cybercab at $29,990 with a $299/month autonomy subscription, targeting December deliveries. The two-seat vehicle lacks a steering wheel and pedals.

items.headline: Tesla Winds Down Cybertruck Production
items.summary: Tesla announced it will cease Cybertruck production at its Austin facility by mid-2027, ending production of the vehicle with disappointing sales.

items.headline: Singtel H1 Underlying Profit Rises 10% to S$1.49 Billion
items.summary: Singtel's H1 underlying net profit grew 10% to S$1.49 billion despite reported net profit falling 55% due to absence of prior-year divestment gains. Interim dividend raised 10% to S$0.09 per share.

items.headline: Singtel Shares Rise 3% on Upgraded Guidance
items.summary: Singtel shares gained 3% in early trade, marking their biggest intraday gain since mid-August, after raising full-year operating company EBIT guidance on strong first-half performance.

items.headline: Singapore Exchange Reports Stronger October Trading Activity
items.summary: Singapore Exchange announced stronger trading in October with increased securities turnover as investors navigated market pullbacks. Derivatives and ETF trading also expanded.

items.headline: US Stocks Close Mixed on Tech Weakness
items.summary: S&P 500 fell 0.4% and Nasdaq declined 0.91% while Dow rose 0.1%, with technology and consumer discretionary sectors lagging while energy and consumer staples led gains.
